stem: Which countries make up Great Britain?
exp: Great Britain is the island of England, Scotland and Wales. The United Kingdom adds Northern Ireland.

opts.t: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland

stem: In which year did the Romans, under Emperor Claudius, invade Britain?
exp: Julius Caesar tried to invade in 55 BC but did not stay. The Romans returned under Emperor Claudius in AD 43 and ruled for about 400 years.

stem: Which Scottish king defeated the English at the Battle of Bannockburn in 1314?
exp: Robert the Bruce defeated the English at Bannockburn in 1314. Scotland stayed unconquered by the English.

stem: Which king was made to agree to the Magna Carta in 1215?
exp: Nobles forced King John to agree to the Magna Carta in 1215. It showed that even the king had to obey the law.

stem: In 1588, which fleet did the English defeat?
exp: The English defeated the Spanish Armada, a large fleet of ships sent to invade England and bring back the Catholic faith.

stem: Who is usually thought of as the first Prime Minister?
exp: Sir Robert Walpole was the first politician to lead the government as Prime Minister. He held the post from 1721 to 1742.

stem: When did fighting in the First World War end?
exp: The First World War ended at 11 am on 11 November 1918. People remember those who died on this date each year.

stem: Who became Prime Minister in 1940 and led Britain in the Second World War?
exp: Winston Churchill became Prime Minister in 1940. His speeches helped people stay strong when Britain stood alone against Germany.

stem: Who was the first woman to be Prime Minister of the UK?
exp: Margaret Thatcher became the UK's first woman Prime Minister in 1979. She led the government until 1990.

stem: Who invented the World Wide Web?
exp: Sir Tim Berners-Lee, a British scientist, created the World Wide Web. Information was first shared on it in 1990.

stem: Who is the patron saint of Scotland?
exp: St Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland and St Andrew's Day is 30 November. St David is for Wales, St George for England and St Patrick for Northern Ireland.

stem: What is New Year's Eve called in Scotland?
exp: In Scotland, 31 December is called Hogmanay. For some Scottish people it is a bigger celebration than Christmas.

stem: Which is the oldest tennis tournament in the world?
exp: The Wimbledon Championships began in 1877. It is the oldest tennis tournament in the world and the only major one played on grass.

stem: Who wrote Oliver Twist?
exp: Charles Dickens wrote many famous novels, including Oliver Twist and Great Expectations. They show the lives of poor people in the 19th century.

stem: Where is the Giant's Causeway?
exp: The Giant's Causeway is on the north-east coast of Northern Ireland. It is made of thousands of six-sided rock columns.

stem: What is the minimum age to vote in a UK general election?
exp: You must be 18 or over to vote in elections to the UK Parliament. In some elections in Scotland and Wales, people can vote at 16.

stem: What is the Prime Minister's official home in London?
exp: The Prime Minister lives and works at 10 Downing Street. The Prime Minister also has a country house called Chequers.

stem: What is the Commonwealth?
exp: The Commonwealth is a voluntary association of countries. Most were once part of the British Empire, and the monarch is its head.

opts.t: An association of countries, most once part of the British Empire
A group of European countries that trade freely
A military alliance of North Atlantic countries
The parliament of the four UK countries

stem: How many people sit on a jury in England, Wales and Northern Ireland?
exp: A jury has 12 people in England, Wales and Northern Ireland. In Scotland a jury has 15 people.

stem: What is the electoral register?
exp: To vote, your name must be on the electoral register. You can register online or through your local council.

opts.t: The official list of people who can vote
A list of everyone who pays tax
